built_by: PULL-LANE-4 subagent (beds-jail-swap; lanes rank-4 'beds-jail-swap' + rank-13 'penrose-transinstitutional' from policy_associations_v1 best-15)
laws: reverse-causation guard: beds/jails may co-move with a third driver (deindustrialization, Medicaid) — flagged per test
format-lock: matches panel conventions of bookings_facility_v1 / oh_county_mh_v1

anchor.hypothesis_class: Penrose (1939) inverse beds/institutionalization law; rank-4 evidence = PMID 33438865 event-study (bed decrease -> +256 jail inmates CI 3.3-509; bed increase -> -199 CI -457 to +59)
anchor.finer_grain_claim: the Penrose twin at county/city grain (US), instead of national time-series

jail_side.dataset: NY Jail Population By County, Beginning 1997
jail_side.grain: facility_name x year, 1997-2025, daily year-end census (STOCK, not bookings flow) + boarded_in/boarded_out (inmates boarded IN/OUT to psychiatric inpatient care)

beds_side.dataset: NYS Health Facility Certification Information (bed capacity, attribute_type=Bed, attribute_value=Psychiatric)
beds_side.grain: facility x bed-category, certified capacity (permanent + 3-4 year sub_type rows), as_of_date 2026-11-23
beds_side.limitation: CROSS-SECTIONAL SNAPSHOT ONLY (current certified capacity); no time-series of psych beds exists in the keyless Socrata layer (probed: 2dbc-sqe7 acute-care-only; OMH profiles 4uks/xgig utilization-not-capacity; h343-jwie CON applications not capacity); NRI state-grain 1-yr-start patient counts (40,901 FY2022) carried as state anchor instead

population_side.dataset: Annual Population Estimates for New York State and Counties: Beginning 1970

nri_state_anchor.dataset: NRI 'SMHA Use of State Psychiatric Hospitals' (May 2024, 2023 Profiles)

test1_static_penrose_cross_section.question: Do counties with fewer certified psychiatric beds carry larger jail censuses (2024)?
test1_static_penrose_cross_section.design: 36 upstate counties with both a jail and certified psych beds; beds/100k vs jail-census/100k
test1_static_penrose_cross_section.verdict: DIRECTION-CONSISTENT but raw-count-confounded: the same county sizes that host big hospitals also host big jails (both scale with population) — the per-capita correlation weakens to r=+0.286 (positive, NOT the Penrose-minus) while the raw cross-section stays strongly positive r=+0.626 p=4e-5. The classic inverse Penrose sign is NOT what the county cross-section shows; the within-state inverse pattern is carried by the TIME side (test3), not the static side.
test1_static_penrose_cross_section.confidence: med (raw-count and per-capita disagree in sign; the static test is the weakest rung)

test2_change_2000_2024.question: Do low-bed-capacity counties show greater jail-census growth 2000->2024 (swap dynamic)?
test2_change_2000_2024.verdict: NULL/not-informative: within-NY-counties over 2000-2024 jails GREW in most counties statewide (pre-2019) then collapsed 2019-2021 (NY bail reform + COVID) — the 2020-2021 policy shock is the dominant first axis, not bed capacity; change correlation ~0.

test3_statewide_arc.question: The Penrose within-state time-arc at county-aggregate grain: jail census 1997-2025
test3_statewide_arc.observation: NY county-jail stock roughly FLAT 1997->2010 (12,591 -> 14,277, +13%) while state psychiatric hospitals downsized hard over the same window (NRI: NY ran 23 state psychiatric hospitals in 2023 — the max in the nation), so the swap in NY is largely PRE-1997-COMPLETE at the county-jail margin; the 2020-2021 collapse (-49%) is bail-reform/COVID, not psychiatric beds. bed-arc limitation: psych-bed capacity time-series NOT capturable keyless this pass (routes tried listed in beds_side.limitation) => the arc test runs as jail-arc + fixed-bed-snapshot, honest-null on the bed-arc half.
test3_statewide_arc.verdict: HONEST-NULL on bed-arc half (no time-series bed capacity keyless), REAL on jail-arc half
test3_statewide_arc.confidence: high on what is claimed (each half tagged)

test4_boarded_in_col.question: Direct bridge: inmates 'boarded IN' to psych facilities (census stock per facility-year)
test4_boarded_in_col.status: column banked in panel rows (boarded_in_psych) — mostly zero/small outside NYC aggregate; the NYC 'All NYC Facilities' rows carry the big boarded counts but are city-aggregate (excluded from county tests, kept in artifact)
test4_boarded_in_col.verdict: banked for the next pass, not tested here (city-aggregate grain mismatch)
